stem: An intestinal transplant recipient calls reporting bleeding from the ostomy site. According to urgent-contact education, how should the coordinator classify this symptom?

options.text: An urgent matter because ostomy bleeding is a listed potential bleeding source requiring prompt team contact
A non-urgent matter to address at the next routine refill call
An expected finding that never requires transplant team notification
A reason to permanently stop all immunosuppression without team guidance

explanation.rationale_correct: Bleeding from ostomy sites is listed among urgent matters requiring prompt transplant team contact, alongside oral, rectal, and wound bleeding sources.

rationale_incorrect.B: Ostomy bleeding is explicitly urgent, not deferred to routine refill calls.
rationale_incorrect.C: Post-transplant teaching requires reporting bleeding from ostomy and other listed sources.
rationale_incorrect.D: Urgent bleeding prompts team evaluation rather than unilateral immunosuppression cessation.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → h. Communication → iii. Urgent matters → Bleeding

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → h. Communication with the transplant team → iii. Urgent matters → Bleeding (ostomy source listed); PDF p. 111 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Seventh 030700 item; intestine ostomy-bleeding angle distinct from oral (cctc-3040), rectal (cctc-3022), and other urgent-contact items; anchor verified on Cupples p. 111.

stem: A transplant recipient on a calcineurin inhibitor is started on an ACE inhibitor for hypertension. Which laboratory abnormality should the coordinator anticipate monitoring?

options.text: Isolated hypoglycemia without any renal effect
Permanent normalization of all electrolytes without monitoring
Guaranteed improvement in graft function without lab review

explanation.rationale_correct: ACE inhibitors used with calcineurin inhibitors require caution because of risk for hyperkalemia and renal insufficiency.

rationale_incorrect.B: The interaction of concern is hyperkalemia and renal insufficiency rather than isolated hypoglycemia.
rationale_incorrect.C: Combined ACE inhibitor and CNI therapy requires electrolyte and renal monitoring rather than assuming normalized labs.
rationale_incorrect.D: Drug combinations may worsen renal function and require monitoring rather than guaranteeing graft improvement.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: ACE inhibitors … Caution when used in combination with CNIs: Risk for hyperkalemia and renal insufficiency

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 4 → CNI-associated hypertension → c.i.ii. ACE inhibitors (hyperkalemia and renal insufficiency risk with CNIs); PDF p. 162 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Seventh 030100 item; hyperkalemia risk with ACE+CNI distinct from urinary-leak labs (cctc-3034) and cholangitis pattern (cctc-3038); anchor verified on Cupples p. 162.

stem: A kidney recipient develops sudden oliguria and rising serum creatinine months after transplant. Which complication should the coordinator include in the differential?

options.text: Obstruction at the ureterovesical anastomotic site
Expected normal healing that never affects urine output
Mandatory graft nephrectomy for every creatinine rise
A complication that can occur only on the day of surgery

explanation.rationale_correct: Obstruction at the anastomotic site can occur any time after transplantation and may present with oliguria or elevation of BUN and/or creatinine, requiring surgical treatment.

rationale_incorrect.B: Oliguria and creatinine rise warrant evaluation for obstruction or other graft problems rather than assumed benign healing.
rationale_incorrect.C: Anastomotic obstruction is evaluated and treated surgically rather than mandating immediate nephrectomy for every creatinine rise.
rationale_incorrect.D: Anastomotic obstruction may occur at any time after transplant, not only on the day of surgery.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 17, Kidney Transplantation → i. Obstruction at the anastomotic site
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Obstruction at the anastomotic site … Presents as oliguria or elevation of BUN and/or creatinine

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 17 → i. Obstruction at the anastomotic site (oliguria or BUN/creatinine elevation any time after transplant); PDF p. 903 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Seventh 030200 item; ureteral obstruction angle distinct from urinary leak (cctc-3035) and rejection fever (cctc-3026); anchor verified on Cupples p. 903.

stem: A recipient on azathioprine develops a low white blood cell count. Which adverse effect profile is MOST consistent with this medication?

options.text: Bone marrow suppression with leukopenia or pancytopenia
Permanent cure of hypertension without hematologic effects
Guaranteed protection against all infections without cytopenias
No hematologic side effects because azathioprine is not immunosuppressive

explanation.rationale_correct: Azathioprine adverse effects include bone marrow suppression resulting in leukopenia, pancytopenia, thrombocytopenia, and/or macrocytic anemia.

rationale_incorrect.B: Azathioprine is immunosuppressive and may cause cytopenias rather than curing hypertension.
rationale_incorrect.C: Immunosuppression increases infection risk; azathioprine may cause leukopenia rather than preventing cytopenias.
rationale_incorrect.D: Azathioprine is an antiproliferative immunosuppressant with recognized bone marrow suppression.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 4, Immunosuppression → e. Azathioprine—Adverse effects → i.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Bone marrow suppression, resulting in leukopenia, pancytopenia, thrombocytopenia

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 4 → e. Azathioprine—Adverse effects → i. (bone marrow suppression with leukopenia/pancytopenia); PDF p. 150 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Seventh 030300 item; azathioprine hematologic toxicity distinct from CNI (cctc-3018/3023), MMF (cctc-3009), and cyclosporine cosmetic effects (cctc-3044); anchor verified on Cupples p. 150.
